decisions.decision: Monthly periods are the phasing granularity.
decisions.note: User chose monthly over the recommended quarterly. Consequence surfaced before the choice: 36 rows per initiative over a 3-year horizon. Accepted, mitigated by D-05 auto-fill.

decisions.decision: Track run-rate (steady-state annual) separately from in-year realized value.
decisions.note: Matches the distinction practitioners treat as essential — an initiative can be at 100% run-rate while in-year banked value is far lower.

decisions.decision: Phasing horizon is 3 years, configurable per deal.
decisions.note: Covers the standard cost-synergy ramp to full run-rate; configurable so a small acquisition is not forced into a full 3-year grid.

decisions.decision: Existing targetM / realizedM become DERIVED TOTALS (rollup of the phased rows), not removed and not independently editable.
decisions.note: Chosen for demo-showcase safety — every existing consumer (demo showcase, PMO console, dashboards) keeps working untouched. The demo is a maintained deliverable per PROJECT.md.

decisions.decision: Monthly rows are generated by ramp-template auto-fill: IL enters run-rate + start month + curve shape (cost 30/70/100, revenue 10/40/70, or linear), rows generate automatically and stay individually editable.
decisions.note: This is what makes monthly granularity workable. Curve shapes taken from standard PMI ramp practice.

decisions.decision: Realized value is editable ONLY for months that have arrived — no forward-booking of value into future months.
decisions.note: Credibility control: forward-booked value is the main way synergy tracking loses trust.

decisions.decision: REPLACE the 5 execution statuses with exactly the 4 SYN-03 confidence stages: idea → validated → committed → captured. One canonical field, one axis.
decisions.note: Mapping applied once: identified→idea, validated→validated, planned+executing→committed, realized→captured. Rejected: a 5-gate rename keeping 'executing' (mixes a confidence axis with an execution state — the thing the stage-gate exists to fix), and a second independent confidenceStage field (two axes to keep in sync, nonsense combinations possible). Costs accepted before choosing: 3 of 5 demo seeds map onto 'committed' (addressed by D-10), 2 new i18n keys × 4 langs added and 3 retired (syn.st_identified/planned/executing/realized), demo.db seed rows rewritten — which per the standing WAL trap means a wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) before committing.

decisions.decision: Stage advancement carries MINIMAL HARD GATES, enforced server-side with a stated rejection reason: 'committed' requires an owner AND a phased target (run-rate + start month, per D-05); 'captured' requires realized value recorded in at least one arrived month (per D-06).
decisions.note: Rejected advisory-only and ungated. Rationale: an ungated stage label is decoration — Phase 7's steerco pack (RPT-03, confidence-stage movement) can only trust stage counts if the gates are real.

decisions.decision: Backward stage movement (de-scoping) is ALLOWED but the server requires a non-empty reason, recorded in the initiative's history alongside the stage change.
decisions.note: Rejected forward-only (would force modelling a separate 'dropped' terminal state) and silent-backward. De-scoping is real; an unexplained demotion is worse than none. Ties directly into the Baseline history area.

decisions.decision: The 5 demo seed initiatives are HAND-TUNED to spread across all four stages (rather than taking the mechanical map verbatim), and carry believable phasing rows.
decisions.note: The demo showcase is a maintained deliverable per PROJECT.md; 3 of 5 identical-looking cards would undersell the new capability. Same migration effort, better showcase.

decisions.decision: HARD CUTOVER — no read-time compatibility shim. The 4 stages become the only accepted values in all three duplicated copies (server.js:3043, validators/workstream.js:114, public/js/execution.js:28-30 incl. SYN_LABELS/SYN_COLORS); legacy values are rejected by the validator.
decisions.note: Verified safe during discussion: data/deals/ is EMPTY — no real-deal database exists yet, so there is no real data to strand. A shim would be permanent dead weight no test could prove unreachable. Migration surface is 5 seed rows in demo.db plus the legacy ma-portal.db copy.

decisions.decision: Baseline history is an EXPLICIT SNAPSHOT model: a `baselines[]` array on the initiative, each entry pinning the full prior target curve + run-rate + stage with who/when/why. NOT a keystroke-level change log.
decisions.note: Separation of concerns, decided deliberately: baselines[] = intentional re-baselining, user-visible, deal-member readable; audit.db = exhaustive forensic record, admin-only, unchanged. Rejected a full history[] array (buries the real signal in typo-correction noise, duplicates audit.db) and deriving from audit.db (would require a rowId filter on queryAudit AND a non-admin deal-scoped read path into a compliance control — its own authz design and threat review, for a computed rather than intentional 'baseline').

decisions.decision: A new baseline version is created by an EXPLICIT re-baseline act at any time, AND is FORCED (with a required reason) for any run-rate or curve-shape change once the initiative has reached 'committed'.
decisions.note: Before 'committed' the numbers are still being worked out, so ordinary edits stay ordinary edits. After 'committed' nothing can be edited quietly — the trail is in-app, not just in audit.db. Rejected explicit-only (a committed target could be silently edited) and automatic-on-any-change (many low-value versions during early entry).

decisions.decision: Baseline v1 is PINNED as the 'deal case' and is never superseded. Variance reports against BOTH the deal case and the current baseline.
decisions.note: This is the number the deal was approved on — losing it behind three re-baselines is how synergy programs stop being accountable. Phase 7 RPT-03 depends on it. Rejected a flat peer-version list.

decisions.decision: AUTHZ: re-baselining is restricted to the Integration Lead and admin, enforced SERVER-SIDE. Baseline history is readable by any authenticated member of that deal.
decisions.note: Stated explicitly rather than left for the planner to infer, because an authz bug has surfaced at the review gate in four consecutive phases (most recently CR-01, where a completion branch checked status but never compared owner to caller). Rejected owner-can-also-re-baseline (weakens the governance meaning AND needs the exact owner-vs-caller comparison the codebase has gotten wrong before) and any-member-writes.

decisions.decision: Staleness is driven by an explicit `lastConfirmedAt` stamp, set by a deliberate 'confirm current' action OR a real value/stage change — but NOT by editing a note or title.
decisions.note: The point of SYN-05 is that someone stands behind the number; a typo fix must not make a six-week-old forecast look confirmed. Works identically at every stage. Rejected period-completeness (says nothing about idea/validated initiatives, which have no realized value yet and would read as permanently stale, and cannot distinguish 'not updated' from 'genuinely zero') and any-write updatedAt (freshness only as honest as the editor). NOTE: no updatedAt/lastConfirmedAt field exists today — this is greenfield.

decisions.decision: Staleness threshold is 30 days, configurable per deal, applied uniformly to every stage.
decisions.note: Matches the monthly phasing cadence of D-01 and the monthly reporting rhythm; one number is also what Phase 7 RPT-04 needs to split current from stale. Rejected stage-dependent defaults (more faithful, but a rule the IL and the steerco pack both have to explain) and 14 days (more items sitting stale at any moment, dulling the signal).

decisions.decision: Stale initiatives are visibly badged AND the headline rollup splits the figure: 'realized $XM, of which $YM unconfirmed'.
decisions.note: Matches SYN-05's own wording — visibly flagged rather than silently trusted — without hiding value, and gives Phase 7 a number to print. Rejected flag-only (a rollup made entirely of stale numbers still presents as one confident figure) and exclude-from-rollup (headline jumps for reasons unrelated to actual value capture).

decisions.decision: Stale initiatives nudge their owner by REUSING the Phase 4 deal-home in-app owner-nudge pattern (DD-02), not a new notification surface.
decisions.note: A flag nobody sees does not change behaviour. Reuses an existing, tested surface rather than inventing a second one.

candidate_extra_areas: Cost-to-achieve treatment (SYN-02) — single figure vs phased monthly alongside the value ramp; how net benefit is computed
Task linkage shape (SYN-04) — one initiative→many tasks vs many-to-many, and whether task completion feeds realized value
canonical_refs: public/js/execution.js:26-30,215-280 (the ONLY synergy UI — third SYN_STATUSES copy plus SYN_LABELS/SYN_COLORS and the render/edit handlers)
db/auditHook.js (append-only audit.db; writeAuditBatch stores before/after JSON per write, queryAudit is the admin-only read path — relevant to Baseline history)
